findings.title: Breaking change in exit code: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3
findings.body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and a new FEATURE_DISABLED constant with value 4 was added. Previously the command actually returned exit code 4 to signal 'recreate upgrade needed', even though the public documentation in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc always described exit code 3 as that case. While this PR brings the code into agreement with the documented contract, it is an observable behaviour change for any consumer that has scripted against the previously-returned exit code (e.g. CI pipelines checking for exit code 4 to detect that a recreate upgrade is required). Because the change to an already-documented/previewed command is made silently in a 'feature flag' PR, reviewers should explicitly call out the swap (4 -> 3 for recreate, 4 now means feature disabled) and ensure this is highlighted in release notes so existing automation can be updated.

findings.title: YAML example contains literal 'Recreate|<not set>' which is not valid YAML
findings.body: In the new Keycloak CR example the value 'strategy: Recreate|<not set>' is shown. The pipe-separated placeholder is a documentation convention indicating 'either Recreate or leave the field unset', but the surrounding block is fenced as [source,yaml] and the value is therefore syntactically invalid YAML (the literal string 'Recreate|<not set>' would be parsed as a strategy value if copy-pasted). A user following the example literally would either get a parse error or end up with the value 'Recreate|<not set>' as the strategy. The PR also re-numbers the callout (now <2>) but does not fix the placeholder. Replace the inline placeholder with a valid example (e.g. 'strategy: Recreate') and describe the default state in prose or in the existing table.

findings.title: Exit-code comment only documents picocli codes 1 and 2, not the new 3 and 4
findings.body: The comment block introduced above the constants reads '// see picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode // 1 -> software error // 2 -> usage error' followed by RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED = 4. The comment implies that 3 and 4 are also picocli exit codes, which they are not - they are now Keycloak-specific values that occupy the same numeric space as picocli-defined codes. Future readers may be confused about the source of these numbers. Either move the explanatory comment to only document the picocli slots (1 and 2) and add a separate note clarifying that 3 and 4 are tool-defined codes, or rename the comment to 'Tool exit codes' and list all four with their meanings.
